subject: Money
title: The Roaring Twenties
description: A quick, practical guide to The Roaring Twenties.

hook.text: The Dow Jones rose 500% between 1921 and 1929. Shoeshine boys gave stock tips. Then came Black Tuesday.

buildup.text: New technologies—radio, cars, electricity—created genuine wealth. But margin buying supercharged speculation.

discovery.text: Investors could buy $100 of stock with just $10 cash. The other $90 was borrowed. Leverage was everywhere.

twist.text: On October 29, 1929, the market lost 12% in one day. By 1932, stocks had fallen 89% from the peak.

climax.text: The crash triggered the Great Depression. Twenty-five percent unemployment. Bank failures nationwide.

punchline.text: The party ended. The hangover lasted a decade.

quiz.question: What amplified the stock market bubble of the 1920s?
options: Buying stocks on margin with borrowed money
